clue.text: Suspicious armed man dropped in with no credentials

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped in by parachute
having no identification papers: NO ID

explanation.surface: A gunman parachuted in without any papers would rightly arouse suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: PARA is short for paratrooper; ID is identification, so 'no credentials' is NO ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranoid person is irrationally distrustful, which is one sense of suspicious.

clue.text: Silver bullet landed accidentally

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a single bullet or shot of ammunition

explanation.surface: A silver bullet, as for werewolves, seems to have struck home by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: AG comes from the Latin argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has run aground has struck the shore or seabed by mishap, an unintended landing.

clue.text: Commander accepts objective plan of action

indicators.note: the commander takes in the other word, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman military commander, a crossword regular
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A commanding officer adopts a goal and draws up a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of things to be done, a programme or plan for a meeting or campaign.

clue.text: Stale or unopened

indicators.note: with its opening letter gone, as a parcel never opened lacks its start

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A short query about whether something is stale or still sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like the conjunction joining two options; it is the heraldic tincture gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Old food or news is no longer fresh, which is what stale means.

clue.text: Bidet Edison designed giving trouble

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new design, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bidet invented by Thomas Edison proves temperamental in use.
explanation.definitionFit: A disobedient child or machine refuses to behave, causing problems for whoever is in charge.

clue.text: Builder's hand really has broken

indicators.note: the second word has broken into the first, splitting it apart

parts.note: a hand is a worker, a man
so means very or really, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A builder's hand has truly been fractured on site.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Builder's' is 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'hand' reads as a body part but means a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who builds in stone or brick.

clue.text: Peg fully lifting a million tonnes?

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a teragram is a million million grams, which is a million tonnes

explanation.surface: A tent peg being hauled out with enormous force.
explanation.walkthrough: A teragram is 10 to the 12 grams; a tonne is a million grams, so it is a million tonnes.
explanation.definitionFit: Peg is a traditional pet form of the given name, so 'Peg fully' asks for the name written out in full.

clue.text: Examine boy brought up in immoral circumstances

parts.note: to scan is to look over closely

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means turned to read upwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Investigating a boy raised in a disreputable household.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgraceful affair or situation that causes public outrage over wrongdoing.

clue.text: Opposing voters minutes out of time

indicators.note: the time letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: the minutes of a meeting are its notes

explanation.surface: Dissenters at a meeting record their objection in the minutes after the clock runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament the noes are those who vote against a motion, as opposed to the ayes.

clue.text: Indicate imminent arrival of wine butt

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a butt is the end or stub of something, as a cigarette butt

explanation.surface: A cask of wine whose delivery is signalled in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' suggests a wine cask alongside 'wine'; here it means a leftover end.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to be a sign or omen of something that is about to happen.

clue.text: Carriage's following river in Russia

parts.note: post- as a prefix means after, following
the Ural flows from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage tracks along a Russian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' is how one carries oneself; the 's makes the definition an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Postural describes posture, the way one holds one's body, which is one's bearing or deportment.

clue.text: Family label vase with identical wrapping

indicators.note: the first word wraps round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: same means identical
an urn is a vase-shaped vessel

explanation.surface: A vase wrapped in matching paper bears a family name tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname is the name shared by a family, the label passed down through generations.

clue.text: Setter's suggestion for bored test solver, say

definitions.meaning: a setter hinting at a homophone of 'bored' would write 'sounding' alongside its soundalike, the plank word
a person on whom one tries out ideas to see how they go down, here someone testing a puzzle

explanation.surface: A setter advises the tester who found the puzzle dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the answer is a clue instruction: a word sounding like 'bored'. Its real sense is a person you test ideas on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding board is a confidant used to try out plans before acting on them, as a test solver tries out a puzzle.

clue.text: Magician has affair with Romeo after brief snog

indicators.note: the rest comes after the shortened word
cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to snog is British slang for to kiss passionately, to neck
a romance is a love affair
R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A conjuror's fling with a lover after a quick kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A necromancer is a sorcerer who claims to talk with the dead, a wizard or practitioner of black magic.

clue.text: Telephone office without coins

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
change is loose coins

explanation.surface: A phone office with no coins for the payphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone exchange is the building where calls were connected, the switching centre of a network.

clue.text: Remove tie from fellow leaving enjoyable party

indicators.note: the fellow leaves, so his letter drops out

parts.note: fun as an adjective means enjoyable
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A man takes off his necktie as he departs a fun party.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or tie is to unfasten it, freeing what it held.

clue.text: A Stella following some light regurgitation

parts.note: taken as written
Stella Cidre is the cider sold under the Stella Artois brand, with the French spelling
the lux is the unit of illuminance, a quantity of light

explanation.surface: A pint of Stella after a light ale brings it all back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stella' suggests the lager; the cider made under the same name gives CIDRE, French for cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid reflux is stomach acid coming back up the gullet, the regurgitation known as heartburn.

clue.text: Like Dorset, remarkably varied

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: the county's name is changed remarkably, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist praises Dorset, an English county on the south coast, for its varied scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of mixed sorts, a miscellaneous selection.

clue.text: Male animal parts defendant used

indicators.note: the animal parts the defendant, splitting it in two

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Animal body parts produced in court as evidence by the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed and 'used' both mean habituated, as in being used to something.

clue.text: Upended apple Tango can contains something related

indicators.note: in a down clue the hidden letters are turned upside down, read upwards
the phrase holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the hidden letters run across these words

explanation.surface: An overturned can of apple Tango, a British fizzy drink, has something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognate is a word or thing sharing an origin with another, a relative.

clue.text: Dog without lead is an irritation

indicators.note: the dog loses its leading letter, as a dog off its lead

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog

explanation.surface: An unleashed dog is a nuisance to passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating tickle of the skin, or figuratively a nagging annoyance.

clue.text: Rather special ties in film noted for actor's dress

parts.note: too means excessively, rather much

indicators.note: the ties are made special, rearranged into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film famous for its star's unusual ties and costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Tootsie (1982) stars Dustin Hoffman as an actor who dresses as a woman to get a part.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1982 comedy is remembered chiefly for its lead in drag, a man disguised in women's clothing.

clue.text: Ruffled young horse hugs rail at the start

indicators.note: the horse hugs the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word supplies its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A spooked young horse presses against the rail as the race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffled' suggests a flustered horse; it is ruffles on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is decorated with frills, gathered ruffles of fabric.

clue.text: Dragoon of note turned to salute

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous cavalryman wheels round to salute.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite greeting, and a salute in its older sense is any greeting.

clue.text: Dog perhaps that's bitten son is an irritation

indicators.note: the pet has its teeth round the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A pet dog that has bitten a boy is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or creature, a nuisance.

clue.text: Springlike as the last ice melts away?

indicators.note: the ice melts and reforms, its letters running into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the answer also happens to lie hidden in 'the last ice', a coincidence of the anagram

explanation.surface: The last frost thaws as the season turns to spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springlike' reads as vernal weather; it means behaving like a spring that stretches back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic returns to shape after stretching, as a coiled spring does.

clue.text: All said visit Rome

indicators.note: spoken, the word for 'all' sounds like a different spelling

parts.note: wholly means entirely, all
to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: Everyone urged to go and see Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the Pope's jurisdiction, so Rome stands for it by metonymy, as Washington for the US government.

clue.text: Hurry, save ten bears

indicators.note: save means except, so everything but this part is kept

parts.note: to hasten is to hurry
taken as written, the very letters removed

explanation.surface: A frantic call to rush and rescue ten bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like rescue; it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a mark or name is to have it, as in 'bears a resemblance'.

clue.text: River pretty muddy in the middle

parts.note: twee is British for affectedly pretty or quaint

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the five-letter word has a single central letter

explanation.surface: A pretty river turns muddy halfway along.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed forms part of the border between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river in the Scottish Borders, so the name is an example of a river.

clue.text: Yankee taken on holiday given a makeover

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a rest is a break, a holiday
Y in the NATO alphabet
led means taken somewhere, guided

explanation.surface: An American on vacation gets a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyled means redesigned, changed in appearance.
